runs.question: What penalty does the NIST AI RMF set for an organization that chooses not to adopt it?

answer.text:
The documents I searched do not state any penalty for an organization that chooses not to adopt the NIST AI RMF. I ran two searches of the AI RMF, and neither returned a passage on penalties, sanctions, or consequences for non-adoption.

What the framework does say is closer to the opposite of a mandate. It describes itself as intended to be flexible and to augment existing risk practices which should align with applicable laws, regulations, and norms. It also notes that use of the AI RMF alone will not lead to these changes or provide the appropriate incentives, which suggests that adoption is left to each organization. Its effectiveness section only encourages users to evaluate whether it has improved their ability to manage AI risks.

The passages do not say whether the framework is legally mandatory for any organization. If you need that, a federal policy document such as the OMB memos in this collection may address it, and I can search those.

support.reason: Passage states the framework is intended to be flexible, augment existing risk practices, and align with applicable laws, regulations, and norms.
Passage states that use of the AI RMF alone will not lead to these changes or provide the appropriate incentives.
Passage says organizations are encouraged to periodically evaluate AI RMF effectiveness; it does not state the claim's inference that adoption is left to each organization.
